claims.explanation: Table 1 (table1_lvlm_robustness.md) reports Avg clean/2/255/4/255 across COCO, Flickr30k, TextVQA and VQAv2 for both OF-9B and LLaVA 1.5-7B. Two aggregating best_baseline_consistency properties are necessary because FARE2 must pair only with TeCoA2 and FARE4 only with TeCoA4; each covers both LVLMs and every clean/attack condition, using reported averages rather than requiring individual-task superiority. E01's clean-all-samples and 500-image adversarial conditions remain those of the source table. The OF-9B FARE2 4/255 condition is retained despite the reported directional discrepancy; no exception, weaker quantifier or verdict-driven repair was introduced.

E06/Table 14 (table14_embedding_loss.md) report mean squared clean and adversarial embedding distortions for both training radii on 500 ImageNet images, with 100-step APGD at attack radius 4/255. Their FARE-versus-TeCoA directions are available, but C02 also says 'significantly' lower and attributes drop-in LVLM replacement without retraining to preservation. No variance, significance criterion or direct causal/retraining measurement is supplied. A reported pairwise mean comparison cannot express that complete statistical-and-enabling assertion; no two-direction-only subclaim is substituted.

E02/Table 3 (table3_targeted_attacks.md) fully identifies six targets, 25 trials per target, both attack radii and FARE2/FARE4, including 0/25 counts and the 2.0% FARE2 mean at 4/255. C03 and its any-success falsifier make absolute zero success substantive, not merely a comparison to TeCoA. The reported-evidence catalog has pairwise directional/ratio relations, not absolute count/rate equality or a zero-success threshold. Comparing FARE to another zero-valued encoder would not establish zero without an independent bound and would add an unclaimed baseline. No measurements were copied into the spec as substitute operands.

E03/Table 4 (table4_zeroshot_classification.md) reports averages over the 13 non-ImageNet datasets, with clean gaps 7.0 and 6.9 percentage points and FARE2 adversarial 43.1% versus TeCoA2 43.6% at 2/255. The full statement asserts additive clean improvements and adversarial comparability; the falsifier's clean direction alone is weaker. Reported relations do not express a fixed additive gap or two-sided equivalence about a reported pair, and no margin defines 'comparable'. Compound consistency's one-sided ID tolerance would not preserve that equivalence conjunct or the two stated clean magnitudes.

E04/Table 5 (table5_pope_hallucination.md) reports clean POPE mean F1 across adversarial/popular/random splits for LLaVA-1.5 7B. C05 expressly reports FARE2 80.8 versus TeCoA2 75.9, FARE4 76.3 versus TeCoA4 72.2 and closeness to original CLIP 84.5. The catalog can compare FARE and TeCoA means, but has no reported-evidence absolute-value assertion or distance-to-a-third-operand relation for this full statement. The simpler higher-mean falsifier does not license silently dropping the stated means and original-CLIP closeness condition.

E04/Table 6 (table6_sqai.md) supplies SQA-I accuracy for original CLIP, FARE2/4 and TeCoA2/4 on clean LLaVA-1.5 7B. C06 asserts the 2.3- and 2.4-percentage-point improvements and the 1.1-point gap below original CLIP, not just higher accuracy than TeCoA. Reported-evidence relations lack additive-difference equality/bounds and scalar-value assertions; ratio comparison is not an additive percentage-point comparison. Declaring only the two gt relations would omit those substantive magnitudes and the original-CLIP condition.

E01/Table 2 (table2_transfer_attacks.md) contains both transfer directions at 4/255; Table 1 supplies clean COCO CIDEr references. The non-robust cross-model values 25.5 versus 115.5 and 8.3 versus 79.7 are identifiable, but the required 'near-clean' result for FARE2 and FARE4 has no tolerance, equivalence margin or attack-success cutoff. The source table includes transfers both below and above clean scores. Choosing a margin after inspecting these differences or simply testing higher-than-nonrobust performance would change the full robustness condition, so the original claim remains skipped.
